turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I’ve been more in front of people at work lately, and I can’t stop focusing on this one part of my face that looks uneven to me, especially in photos. Other people say they barely notice it, but I just keep staring at it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent focus on a perceived uneven facial feature that others reportedly barely notice, especially when viewing photos.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself doing things like checking mirrors, taking photos, or asking others for reassurance about how that part of your face looks, and if so, how much time each day would you say you spend on that?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. Before I send event photos or get on a meeting with a vendor, I’ll keep checking myself in my phone camera. I retake pictures, tilt my head different ways, and sometimes ask a coworker if I look weird. It can take long enough that I get behind on my planning work.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports repeated phone-camera checking, retaking photos, changing head position, and seeking coworker reassurance about appearance, causing delays in work planning.

turns.doctor_question: If you didn't have this worry about your face at all, do you think you'd still feel anxious or nervous being in front of people at work and in meetings?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I mean, meetings can be a little stressful anyway, but I don’t know if I’d feel this nervous about being in front of people without worrying about my face.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel nervous or anxious in work situations where your appearance isn't visible at all—like a phone call or an email exchange with a vendor—or does the anxiety mainly come up when you can be seen?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I feel anxious on phone calls or emails in the same way. I just know it gets much worse when I know someone can see me.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from worries about how your face looks, do you ever feel anxious about being judged or evaluated by others in social or work situations—like giving a presentation or having your ideas critiqued—even when your appearance isn't a factor?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about whether I’m anxious about my ideas being judged separately from how I look. I just notice the face thing most when I’m around people.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself checking or worrying about that part of your face even when you're alone at home, with no one around to see or judge you?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, sometimes. I’ll check my face in my phone camera a lot, especially before a vendor meeting or before I send out event pictures. I’ll retake photos, tilt my head different ways, and sometimes ask a coworker if I look weird. It can take up so much time that I end up behind on my planning work.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports repeated phone-camera checking, retaking photos, altering head position, and seeking reassurance from a coworker about facial appearance, with interference in work planning.
